column1: # Written by Claude (origin "claude"). One line per entry:  entry id|typical learner mistake|usage note
# Notes are in English. Either text column may be empty.
sv:du:pronoun||Swedes say du to almost everyone, including strangers and bosses. Ni for one person is rare and can sound old-fashioned.
sv:ni:pronoun||Ni is mainly the plural "you".
sv:sin:pronoun|Sin, sitt, sina refer back to the subject: "Han tar sin bok" (his own book); "han tar hans bok" means someone else's.|
sv:bli:verb||Bli means to become, and with a past participle it makes the passive: "boken blev skriven".
sv:få:verb||Få means to get or receive, and to be allowed to: "Får jag komma in?"
sv:gift:adjective|Gift means married. As a noun, ett gift is poison.|
sv:rolig:adjective|Rolig means fun or funny, not calm (lugn).|
sv:semester:noun|Semester means holiday or vacation, not a school term (termin).|
sv:fika:noun||A coffee break, usually with something sweet: a Swedish social habit.
sv:lagom:adverb||Not too much and not too little: just right.
sv:tack:interjection||Tack is thanks, and it is also how you accept something: "Ja, tack" (yes, please).
sv:väl:adverb||Väl turns a statement into an expected agreement: "Du kommer väl?" (You're coming, right?)
sv:ju:adverb||Ju marks something both people know: "Det vet du ju" (you know that, after all).
sv:inte:adverb|In a main clause inte comes after the verb ("jag talar inte"), in a subordinate clause before it ("att jag inte talar").|
sv:man:pronoun||Man means "one, people" in general: "man säger att …".
sv:snäll:adjective||"Var snäll och …" is a polite way to ask: please …
sv:kunna:verb||Kunna also means to know a language or a subject: "jag kan svenska".
sv:veta:verb|Veta is for facts; for people and places use känna: "jag känner honom".|
sv:känna:verb|Känna is to know a person or a place, and also to feel: "jag känner mig trött".|
